messages:
hana: Thinking out loud about a lightweight tensor-index file to speed up partial loads for safetensors + mixed sharding. want feedback on tradeoffs.

deepak: TL;DR: small index per checkpoint listing (tensor_name -> byte_range, shape, dtype, optional checksum). runtime can mmap + read only needed ranges.

hana: exactly. current problem: with large single-file safetensors you either parse headers (costly) or mmap whole file then scan at runtime. index lets runtime avoid parse and enables cheap range requests for streaming.

oliver: two quick questions: 1) where to store the index? sidecar object vs embedded footer? 2) what about authenticity? index must match checkpoint.

hana: sidecar preferred: keeps original safetensors untouched (no format tinkering), works with existing tooling. sidecar named checkpoint.id.index.json. for authenticity we sign the index and include signature in commit metadata. runtime validates signature against checkpoint id.

deepak: sidecar also lets us store multiple indexes for different sharding strategies (device-aligned vs layer-aligned). good for experiments.

safu-checker: security note: if we accept sidecars from external parties, must validate they reference canonical offsets and sizes that exist. otherwise a malicious index could trick runtime into wrong range reads. verify via committed file-size and checksums.

hana: agreed. propose index schema minimal: [ {"tensor":"wte.weight","offset":"12345","length":"54321","dtype":"f32","shape":"[32000,768]","sha256":"..."}, ... ] as JSON lines. keep it tiny.

oliver: json lines ok, but prefer compact binary index for very large models to reduce extra IO. protobuf or flatbuffers?

hana: binary option ok, but we should ship human-readable fallback. most index sizes small (<1% of checkpoint).

deepak: tradeoff: per-tensor checksums allow granular corruption detection but cost to compute during ingest. can be async. should we make per-tensor checksum optional?

safu-checker: make it policy-driven. default: compute per-tensor checksum for >256MB tensors or when require_tensor_checksums flag is set. otherwise compute file-level checksum.

hana: streaming scenario: index + signed shard URLs -> client can request only ranges for tensors needed for warmup/prefix caching. runtime can prefetch first-N layers concurrently. this shrinks warmup latency for small prompts.

oliver: thinking about io alignment: many devices prefer memory aligned pages. if index returns arbitrary offsets, runtime will still do page-aligned reads and waste IO. solution: index should include 'preferred_alignment' and 'pad_start' to indicate an aligned range to grab.

hana: good point. include 'read_window': {start, end} computed at ingest time based on heuristics (tensor boundary + alignment). keeps runtime simpler.

deepak: sharding angle: if checkpoint is sharded, index entries should include shard_id so runtime can request from correct object store path. also allow 'fallback_shards' for replicated shards.

safu-checker: and for encrypted shards, index should include 'encryption_meta' pointer to key-tag and IV. runtime will fetch key material via KMS and stream-decrypt. ensure KMS policy check before exposing plaintext ranges.

hana: performance concern: adding index increases ingest latency. mitigation: build index in background and mark checkpoint as 'indexing: pending' while allowing runtime to access whole-file stream; runtime will prefer committed+indexed artifacts for fastest warmup.

oliver: wonders about migration: existing checkpoints without index should be marked legacy and runtime should fall back to header-parse path. add metric "index_hit_rate" to track benefit.

deepak: operational: store indexes in same bucket with lifecycle rules. add a validation job that cross-checks index offsets vs object size+sha256. store validation logs per-checkpoint.

safu-checker: I'll add the signing flow: ingest-worker computes index -> signs using KMS key with associated salt-> writes signature to metadata. runtime validates signature with public key cached in config and rejects mismatches.

hana: last topic: micro-shards vs monolithic. index makes micro-shards less necessary because you can stream exact tensor ranges. downside: range requests have higher metadata overhead vs separate shard objects.

oliver: agree. suggestion: hybrid: use device-aligned shards (few hundred MB) plus index for intra-shard tensor ranges. keeps number of objects limited while enabling fine-grained streaming.

hana: ok action items: 1) proto index schema (jsonl + optional binary), 2) ingestion staging job to compute per-tensor offsets + read_window, 3) signature + KMS flow, 4) runtime API: GET /checkpoint/{id}/index and GET /checkpoint/{id}/index/{tensor} -> returns range metadata, 5) metrics + migration plan.

deepak: I'll spin a spike for the staging job and test with a 70B safetensors single-file export.

oliver: I'll sketch runtime read_window consumer and alignment heuristics.

safu-checker: I'll write the KMS signing + verification steps and policy gating.

hana: awesome. if spike looks good i'll fold into the ingest RFC as an optional artifact. thanks all :rocket:
